findings: no-map-parseint-callback: clean first-ever review. Grepped ~75 live parseInt( call sites in actions/setup/js - all pass an explicit radix, none bare-passed to .map(), no aliased `const x = parseInt` indirection either. Zero live misfires.

require-finite-check-before-date-toisostring: clean first-ever review. All live `new Date(dynamicArg).toISOString()/.toJSON()` sites (report_ast.cjs:434/467, check_stop_time.cjs:95, create_project_status_update.cjs:242, expired_entity_cleanup_helpers.cjs:34, ephemerals.cjs:67/83) are guarded either by a direct Number.isNaN(x.getTime()) check or by upstream validation in extractExpirationDate() that returns null before any unguarded use is reached. The rule's own documented scope limit (variable-bound Date receiver not flagged, only inline new Date(x).toISOString() chains) has zero live misses.

no-split-filter-trim-without-trim-map: first-ever review. Rule correctly fires (true positive, not a rule gap) on redact_secrets.cjs:688 and :778 - both `split(",").filter(name => name.trim())`. Line 688's result feeds an UNTRIMMED secretName into `SECRET_${secretName}` lookup at line 690, meaning a GH_AW_SECRET_NAMES value like 'FOO, BAR' silently fails to redact the custom secret BAR (leading-space env var name never matches). Real app-level bug surfaced incidentally; out of eslint-factory issue scope (app code not rule code), flagged in discussion report only. Two structural rule gaps found but zero live grounding: (1) isSplitSeparator only accepts string-literal delimiters, not regex literals, so `.split(/,\s*/).filter(x=>x.trim())` would escape detection; (2) isTrimmedNonEmpty unwraps `!` negation but not a `Boolean(x.trim())` wrapper. Neither combination found live in corpus - not filed.

no-ad-hoc-jsonl-parser: lighter pass only, deferred to next run. 69 files touch jsonl_helpers.cjs; rule's own test suite (32 cases) already covers alias chains, ESM imports, destructuring, computed member access, parser-restart detection - unusually mature for a first review.
